title: reduce streaming token latency: optimize token loop, flush cadence, and backpressure
author: Priya Malhotra
description:
Motivation:
Streaming token latency spikes observed under medium concurrency workloads (10-50 req/s) were traced to: 1) token emission loop holding on small micro-batches while waiting for timer expiry, 2) flush cadence tuned for throughput rather than tail latency, and 3) lack of adaptive backpressure between request queues and the polling/emit loop. This PR introduces a set of coordinated runtime changes to reduce per-token latency and tail variance for streaming responses while preserving overall throughput.

Summary of changes:
- Token loop: switch to an event-driven loop that wakes on (a) new token arrival, (b) explicit flush triggers, or (c) a short adaptive sleep. This reduces unnecessary timer waits for small bursts.
- Flush cadence: introduce dynamic flush windows per-stream based on recent token inter-arrival times (EWMA). Fast streams get sub-ms flushes; slow streams use slightly longer batching to amortize kernel overhead.
- Backpressure: implement queue-depth based backpressure and a soft-cap on inflight micro-batches. If per-worker queue depth exceeds thresholds, upstream request routing will switch to larger-batch path or temporarily shed low-priority requests.
- Continuous batching/scheduling: prioritize low-latency kernels for short sequence/step calls; adjust batch-formation heuristics to prefer completing existing micro-batches if that reduces head-of-line latency.
- KV cache prefetch: prefetch top-k KV segments for predicted next-token ranges for long context windows to reduce occasional cache misses that cause token latency hiccups.
- Metrics and tests: add fine-grained streaming latency histograms (p50/p95/p99 per-token), backpressure event counters, and e2e synthetic bench that simulates real-world inter-arrival distributions.

Implementation notes:
- The token loop change is intentionally conservative: it maintains existing correctness and backoff semantics but replaces the fixed sleep with an event composite (new_token || flush_timer || adaptive_sleep). The adaptive_sleep is clamped to [0.2ms, 6ms] and tuned via EWMA of inter-token gaps.
- Flush window EWMA alpha=0.2 by default; configurable per-deployment via runtime flag `streaming.flush_ewma_alpha` and per-model override in model config.
- Backpressure thresholds are soft by default (configurable): queue_high=512, queue_warn=384, soft_inflight_cap=64. When exceeded we emit a backpressure metric and signal routing.
- Kernel selection: add a short-path kernel marker for short generations (<32 tokens remaining and sequence_len<=512) to avoid heavier vectorized kernels that have larger startup latency.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for token loop and flush window math
- [x] Integration tests for backpressure signalling and route fallback
- [x] Synthetic bench and latency metric dashboards
- [x] Docs: runtime flags and model config notes (redwood/docs streaming section)

Why this is safe to roll out:
- Feature gated behind runtime flag `streaming.adaptive_flush=true` and default-off for Dedicated/Private customers. Gradual rollout via canary on 5% of traffic is supported by the included rollout manifest.
- Changes are additive and do not alter model outputs. KV prefetch is read-only and conservative (no eviction semantics changed).

Risks and mitigation:
- Over-aggressive flushes could reduce throughput on high-traffic long-generation workloads; mitigation: per-model override and automated rollback on throughput regression alerts.
- Backpressure mis-tuning could cause request shedding; mitigation: soft thresholds and metrics before action.

Related work: refs to previous PRs that addressed similar symptoms: pr-18427, pr-19642, pr-20513, pr-21456, pr-23804.

release_notes: Reduce streaming per-token latency by introducing an event-driven token emitter, adaptive flush windows, queue-depth backpressure, and short-path kernel selection. Adds metrics and rollout manifest. Default feature gated.
notes: Canary rollout on 5% traffic; monitor streaming.per_token.p99 and backpressure.route_fallback metrics for first 48h.
perf_results_summary: Synthetic bench shows median per-token latency reduction of ~22% and p99 improvement of ~35% on mixed inter-arrival workload. Throughput impact within 3% on long-generation heavy workloads when adaptive flush is enabled per-model.
